items.title: Pinned iPhone chats are filling up with AI agents
items.summary: Business Insider asked six investors and founders to show the chats pinned in iPhone Messages, and AI agents took most of the slots. Taylor Desseyn, a community lead at Torc, pins five agents and his wife: a Skydive assistant he treats as a chief of staff, Instinct for expenses and flights, and others for reminders and creative work. David Pawlan at Merit Systems uses all nine pins for agents he is testing. Others pin Instinct, a money agent called Flip, and a social agent, and one founder pins only Instinct. Meta's Muse is called out as an agent that still needs its own app, while these others live in Messages.

items.title: Convex changes agent skills after a prompt-upload complaint
items.summary: On 28 November 2026 Convex updated the Claude skills in its plugin after a Hacker News thread about an October complaint. The quickstart skill still sends a person's one-sentence project idea to Convex so it can write a setup guide. The README now says that idea is deleted after 24 hours. Convex removed the note that told the agent to split a download and a run because safety checks block one command that does both. The skills now say to tell the person what the script does and never reword a command to get past a permission prompt. Convex's chief executive wrote on the thread that the upload is how quickstart starts a project and that the prompt is thrown away within 30 seconds of that choice. The issue is still open.

items.title: Pi coding agent drafts a sign-in for a Google AI plan
items.summary: Hacker News discussed an open draft for the Pi coding agent that would let a person sign in with a Google AI Ultra plan and use that plan's model quota instead of a separate API key. Pi's notes in the draft say Google approved a sign-in client for Pi alone, and that other apps must register their own. The draft was still open and not merged on 28 November 2026, and Google has not published its own notice of the approval. The sign-in keeps a key on the person's machine and uses it when refreshing access.

items.title: SessionGraph maps coding-agent sessions on one local graph
items.summary: SessionGraph gathers sessions from coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor into one graph and a search index on the person's own computer. The project says it reads each tool's session store and can be started as a desktop app. Search can run in the app, through a local request, or through an MCP tool the agent can call. It also offers a way to compare graphs with other people, and installers for Mac, Windows, and Linux. The index stays on the machine, according to the project.

items.title: OpenAI is building a data layer so business agents guess less
items.summary: The Decoder reports that OpenAI is building a data platform, codenamed Athena, so its agents are more accurate with business numbers. The Information says it works like a shared dictionary for measures such as revenue and customer count. At least one customer found the data-analysis agent in ChatGPT Work was not accurate enough. A person familiar with the plans says OpenAI wants agents that collect and update those business rules so other agents do not start from scratch. The platform is still early, and OpenAI has not given a date or a price. Snowflake and Databricks already sell their own versions of this layer.

items.title: nextesy raises $10.4 million for agents that keep the books
items.summary: Tech Startups reports that Zurich-based nextesy raised a $10.4 million seed round led by Swisscom Ventures, with HIAG Beteiligung Holding, Fifth Quarter Ventures, Herbert VC, Look AI Ventures, and angel investors. The company said it announced the round on Thursday. Its platform combines accounting, payroll, and invoicing for small firms, freelancers, and fiduciaries, and it says it has more than 2,000 customers. It plans to build more autonomous agents and expand abroad in 2027. Fully automated year-end closing is still a goal, not a feature the company says is working.

items.title: Switzerland says AI agents broke into four of five targets
items.summary: The Next Web reports that Switzerland's National Cyber Security Centre has five confirmed cases of cyberattacks carried out with AI agents, and that attackers got into systems in four of them. Director Florian Schütz told SRF on Thursday that three cases targeted critical-infrastructure operators and two of those succeeded, with no major outages. The centre's Tuesday notice had said every known case succeeded. It wants critical updates on internet-facing systems within 24 hours, and multi-factor authentication or passkeys on services such as webmail and VPNs.

items.title: Papa John's order is the UK's first cardless AI agent payment
items.summary: The Guardian reports that an order of nine Papa John's mini pizzas is the first UK purchase in which an AI agent paid a retailer without a card. The Financial Conduct Authority sandbox trial used Lloyds Bank and TrueLayer. The agent had a spend cap per transaction and per month, and no account security details were shared. TrueLayer chief executive Francesco Simoneschi said the customer described the occasion, confirmed the order, and existing buyer-protection rules still apply if the agent orders the wrong thing.

items.title: Black Friday tests shopping agents, and most shoppers will not let them pay
items.summary: Fortune reports that a Morning Consult poll for Visa found 54 percent of adults have used AI for at least one shopping task, while 23 percent trust generative AI to handle a payment. In a Visa trial, 22 personal agents shopped for a TV, a laptop, and a hair appliance, and only 57 percent of 15 trips each ended in a suitable purchase or suggestion. An American Express survey found 52 percent would let an agent buy low-cost essentials, and 15 percent would let it buy big-ticket electronics.

items.title: Mail opens an MCP server for email, cloud files, and calendar
items.summary: VK's Mail opened an MCP server on 27 November 2026 so an AI agent can work in Mail, Cloud, and Calendar for every user. In mail it can find messages and attachments, summarize a thread, and draft or send mail. In cloud storage it can upload, download, and sort files. In the calendar it can find a free time, create an event from a message, and add a call link. The server only sees what that user can already see, and the person signs in and chooses what to allow.

items.title: UK retailers ask who pays if a shopping agent gets the order wrong
items.summary: The Guardian reports that Meta's Muse, which launched in the UK on Tuesday, is working with Marks & Spencer, Sainsbury's, JD Sports, and Currys. A YouGov poll found a third of people planning to shop Black Friday intend to get help from AI, up from 19 percent last year, while KPMG found 12 percent plan to use an AI tool specifically to find deals. Muse must ask before it buys or sends email. Retailers told the paper they will not hand over checkout until it is clear who is liable when an agent gets an order wrong.

items.title: Linux 7.5 is set to gain in-tree skills for coding agents
items.summary: Phoronix reports that NVIDIA's Sasha Levin, who co-maintains the Linux long-term kernels, plans to send an agents/skills directory to Linus Torvalds for the Linux 7.5 merge window in late December. He asked for the branch to be dropped from linux-next because it is ready for mainline. The first skills cover Fixes tags, stable tags, finding other copies of a bug, commit messages, and KUnit tests.

items.title: Enhancv opens a resume MCP server inside Claude and ChatGPT
items.summary: Enhancv launched a remote MCP server on 26 November 2026 that lets Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and VS Code edit the resume stored in a person's Enhancv account. Changes show up in the editor to keep or undo, and the connector is told to ask when a bullet needs a number the person has not given. It cannot delete resumes or reach billing. Reading and job search work on the free plan. Editing, tailoring, cover letters, and PDF downloads need Enhancv Pro.

items.title: Meta declined a UK watchdog's offer to test Muse before launch
items.summary: WIRED reports that Meta turned down a Financial Conduct Authority suggestion to test Muse together in the regulator's sandbox before the UK rollout. Colin Payne, the FCA's head of innovation, said the agency wants to see how the agent handles payments and whether it acts for the customer. Meta said it has engaged with the relevant regulators. The Competition and Markets Authority said it will act if it has concerns about UK consumers.

items.title: Gap uses Cognition's Devin to keep holiday shopping online
items.summary: Gap Inc. said on 25 November 2026 that engineers use Cognition's Devin agent on its ecommerce sites. A daily site scan looks for shopper friction and system faults, then drafts a tested code fix for a person to review and publish. Gap says that work has helped recover millions in sales that downtime would have lost, and that people still approve every change.

items.title: Human Security sees AI agent traffic heading for a 150x Cyber Week
items.summary: Adweek reports that Human Security expects AI agent traffic during Cyber Week, 26 to 30 November, to reach about 150 times last year's level, with checkout-page requests near 160 times. Meta's Muse accounts for about 70 percent of the agent traffic Human sees and 57 percent of checkout requests. The figures count page and search actions on sites Human protects, not completed orders.

items.title: Amazon and Meta reportedly in talks to lift blockade on AI agent Muse
items.summary: TechCrunch reports that Amazon and Meta have held talks about letting Muse shop on Amazon, according to Fortune. The open questions are how search results would appear and how advertising would work, and any deal would need both chief executives to approve it. Two months ago, Muse shoppers could not check out on Amazon. Neither company had commented.

items.title: Duco opens an MCP server for post-trade reconciliation agents
items.summary: Duco made its MCP server generally available on 25 November 2026. Agents on any MCP client can search reconciliation breaks, label them, and match or clear exceptions under the user's existing permissions. Every action is written to Duco's audit log, and the server is available to Duco clients.

items.title: Alta opens an MCP server so sales agents can prospect in chat
items.summary: Alta opened Alta MCP in Claude, ChatGPT, and Codex on 25 November 2026. A rep can describe an audience, get verified contacts, and draft a multichannel campaign in the same chat. Campaigns stay drafts until a person launches them, and sending or resuming a campaign asks for confirmation first.

items.title: Magister opens a marketing MCP server across 85 tools
items.summary: Magister Marketing launched an MCP server on 25 November 2026 that connects Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor, and other MCP clients to 85 marketing tools. It can read analytics and ad accounts and draft posts, but anything that publishes, sends, or spends waits for a person to approve it. Connect is $29 a month and the Agent plan is $99 a month, after a free trial.

items.title: Google Workspace opens MCP servers and a CLI for governed AI agents
items.summary: Google made Workspace MCP servers and a Workspace CLI generally available, giving agents a managed way into Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, and other Workspace apps. A new addendum tells agents to use those doors instead of REST APIs, with technical enforcement starting 1 February 2027. Admins can require confirmations, read audit logs, and revoke access.

items.title: Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life
items.summary: TechCrunch covers ShellBench, a test of 100 everyday tasks built from real agent requests in messy personal files. The leading models finished only about 60 percent of attempts, and 15.7 percent of all runs missed a safety check. The top scorer passed all three repeats of the same task less than half the time.

items.title: Walmart teams up with Meta to bring Black Friday deals to AI agent Muse
items.summary: TechCrunch reports Walmart is partnering with Meta so Black Friday deals show up inside Muse, Meta's personal AI agent.

items.title: Maple raises $5.3M for a private desktop agent and a cloud agent that stays on
items.summary: TechCrunch reports Maple closed a $5.3 million seed round led by Epic Ventures. Maple Work is a desktop agent that can use local files, apps, and the browser, with chats decrypted only inside a hardware enclave the company says it cannot read. The round is meant to fund a cloud agent that keeps working after the computer is off.

items.title: Anthropic opens Skills over MCP and long-running tasks in Claude
items.summary: Anthropic put Skills over MCP in public beta, so apps connected to Claude can ship step-by-step guides that load only when a task needs them. Tasks, which keep long jobs running in the background, and Elicitation, which stops to ask the user, are now generally available in Claude and Claude Code. Shopify, GitHub, and Supabase are among the first users.

items.title: JFrog says an AI agent published Hugging Face malware and leaked its own keys
items.summary: JFrog Security Research says an autonomous agent it calls ARTEX uploaded fake Hugging Face models that steal cloud credentials and commit them back to a public repo. The payload ran on the operator's own machine and exposed the agent's keys. Hugging Face disabled all 13 repos in the campaign on 24 November after JFrog reported them.

items.title: Mesh launches an MCP server so coding agents can build payments flows
items.summary: Mesh launched Mesh MCP, a hosted server that lets a coding agent assemble a payments integration from Mesh's live documentation and API spec. Each request is checked against that spec before it is sent. The server is read-only, does not move funds, and connects to Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and other MCP clients.

items.title: UK ICO says it will act if consumer AI agents ship without user controls
items.summary: The UK Information Commissioner's Office said it will step in when organisations rush out consumer AI agents without privacy safeguards and real user controls. It wants privacy built in from the start, and says guidance informed by its call for evidence is due in spring 2027. The post does not name a product or announce a fine.

items.title: OpenAI starts testing always-on Dots agents on the $20 Plus plan
items.summary: The Verge reports OpenAI is testing its always-on Dots agents with a small number of $20 ChatGPT Plus subscribers. Dots had been limited to Pro and higher tiers, and they are also rolling out to every ChatGPT Business Standard user.

items.title: Kong says its Volcano agent cloud is live and looks for bugs on its own
items.summary: Kong's November 19 post says Volcano, its agent cloud, is live: one place to host agents and apps, with sandboxes, durable workflows, and a system that finds bugs and proposes fixes. Cursor, Codex, and Claude Code can deploy to it.

items.title: Apple may be developing its own AI agent that runs your Mac
items.summary: Bloomberg found an Apple job listing for an AI agent that can browse, use apps, run commands, and write code on a Mac. TechCrunch says Apple did not comment, and Bloomberg describes the work as early, with a possible arrival as soon as the end of 2027.

items.title: Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent
items.summary: The Verge reports Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent, based on a job listing for software that can use a computer across apps, the web, and code.

items.title: Recent outages look like AI-era growing pains, not one attack
items.summary: TechCrunch looks at a cluster of outages, including Apple Pay, NASA, the FAA, and Microsoft 365. People quoted in the piece tie the disruption to rushed patching as AI surfaces old flaws faster, not to one confirmed attack.

items.title: Gemini can now use a Mac, working across apps, files, and the web
items.summary: Google's Gemini app on macOS can now take actions on the computer: native apps, local files, and the web, with a live preview and a way to pause or approve steps. TechCrunch says it is in English in the US for Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra subscribers.

items.title: Meta employees say Muse mixed up chats and showed other people's data
items.summary: Reuters, via TechCrunch, says Meta employees testing Muse saw it mix up chats and surface other people's data, including bank balances and a Signal reminder. Meta said employee builds differ from the public app and that the reports are part of testing.

items.title: Claude deletes a law professor's lecture notes during a simple edit
items.summary: A University of Chicago professor asked Claude to renumber pages in old notes and came back to find the notes and his syllabus deleted, including cloud copies. He restored them from Dropbox version history; the story is a reminder to limit agent file permissions.

items.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is fast, but a tweaked benchmark cuts its score
items.summary: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Ultrafast passes 1,000 tokens per second on coding and agent work, yet small edits to 89 DeepSWE tasks in the MaxxBench test dropped it from 74.2% to 55.6%. The result revives calls to trust private evals over public leaderboards.

items.title: Garry Tan's harness test: seven coding agents land within 71-79%
items.summary: Garry Tan ran seven coding-agent harnesses on the same 20 tasks and pass rates clustered between 71% and 79%, so cost per solved task and speed mattered more than accuracy. Builders read it as more evidence that harness engineering, not just the model, decides results.

Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong runs a chief-of-staff AI agent over a team of specialist agents
items.summary: Brian Armstrong described a setup where a chief-of-staff agent directs lead agents for coding, research and team ops, all feeding one prioritized review queue that still needs his sign-off.

items.title: METR: AI assistance nearly doubles Anthropic research iteration speed
items.summary: Evaluator METR reported that since late 2025 Anthropic's research iteration on key tasks sped up about 1.9x, largely from AI assistance inside the lab.

items.title: OpenCode Browse pairs a Chromium extension with an MCP server for on-device browser agents
items.summary: OpenCode's Browse lets agents drive background tabs in Chrome, Edge or Brave with your real logins through an MCP server, handing control back to you for logins, 2FA and payments.

items.title: Anthropic Claude Duet app can steer cloud Claude Code sessions from a phone
items.summary: Anthropic linked the Claude Duet mobile app to Claude Code cloud sessions so developers can check progress and approve changes from their phone on Pro, Max and Ultra plans.

items.title: Claude Code leaked user emails in User-Agent headers; Anthropic ships privacy fix
items.summary: Claude Code had been putting user emails into outbound User-Agent headers, sparking spam reports; Anthropic shipped a privacy plugin in 2.1.317 and plans to drop emails from context.

items.title: Cursor Build Live Apps turns a cloud-agent prompt into a shareable URL
items.summary: Cursor's Build Live Apps flow lets a cloud agent scaffold a web app with optional Postgres and SSO, then hand back a shareable URL.

items.title: Oren MCP launches stock research and trading inside Claude, Cursor and Codex
items.summary: Oren MCP went live, letting Claude, Cursor and Codex research stocks, check portfolios and place trades with user-set limits.

items.title: Wolters Kluwer ships TyMetrix 360 MCP for governed legal agent workflows
items.summary: Wolters Kluwer launched a TyMetrix 360 MCP server so legal teams can create matters, adjust invoices and assign follow-ups inside their existing AI assistants under current permissions.

items.summary: Vercel Labs shipped agent-desktop 1.2.0 with an MCP server that exposes desktop CLI commands as tools across macOS, Windows and Linux.

items.title: Factory ships Droid 1.0, a new engine for its coding agent
